Hi Simon — great to chat earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery on security/compliance so your procurement and security teams can triage.

Recap (short):
- You mentioned MedReva will require a vendor security questionnaire to start procurement; preference leaned toward a SIG-compatible spreadsheet but procurement may also accept CAIQ outputs.
- HIPAA/BAA is a firm requirement for any PHI flows; SOC 2 Type II report expected to be relevant for risk review. You said SOC 2 is "in process" and expected next quarter.
- Data residency: US-only environments for now.

Proposed next steps:
1) I can prefill the SIG spreadsheet with answers for the controls that map to Redwood hosted offering and mark evidence placeholders — attach: Redwood_SOC2-summary.pdf and a draft answer doc.
2) Please confirm the scope: API-only (no persistent PHI storage) vs API + optional data-at-rest in your environment.
3) Confirm evidence owners (procurement/legal + security contact) and timeline — our suggested target: return prefilling + any clarifying Qs by EOD 2026-12-17 to keep your pilot timeline intact.
4) If you need a BAA, please share the legal contact and we’ll route to contracts immediately.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2-summary.pdf (summary), I’ll upload a prefilling template if SIG is preferred — otherwise tell me the CAIQ/custom form you want us to use.

Thanks — I’ll wait for confirmation on scope and legal contact and will start prefilling once you confirm SIG vs CAIQ.

—Karthik

Karthik — thanks for the summary and for moving quickly. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Questionnaire type: Procurement prefers SIG (spreadsheet) because it maps to our internal tooling, but if Redwood can also return a CAIQ export that’s helpful for a second review. SIG first please.
2) SOC 2: we need an attested SOC 2 Type II report or, at minimum, the SOC 2 summary + controls mapping to evidence. You mentioned SOC 2 is in process — can you provide an expected audit completion quarter and any interim artifacts?
3) HIPAA / PHI: MedReva will process limited PHI in pilot scenarios. We will need a BAA in place before production. Please route BAA requests to priya.anand@medreva.com (legal).
4) Data residency: US-only — confirmed.
5) Technical clarifications needed upfront (our security team asks these before we accept prefilling):
   • Encryption at rest: what algorithm, KMS options, and do you support customer-managed keys?
   • Network isolation: ability to restrict egress, VPC peering options, private endpoints?
   • Multitenancy: single-tenant/tenant isolation details for the Dedicated/Private options.

If Redwood can provide a prefilling of the SIG sheet and a short "top 10 controls" one-pager that maps to evidence, we can accelerate review. Target timeline: procurement review starting week of 2026-12-20.

Also attaching MedReva_SIG_Request_v1.xlsx — please fill or indicate which rows require evidence upload.

—Simon

Thanks Simon — got it. A couple of clarifying questions before we start prefilling so we align answers and evidence owners:

A) Scope
   1) Will the pilot stream transient PHI only (ephemeral tokens, no persistent storage) or will you be storing PHI in MedReva-managed buckets for the pilot? (affects retention/pseudonymization controls)
B) Evidence owners and delivery
   2) Who at MedReva should receive evidence artifacts? (Priya for legal/BAA; procurement@medreva.com for checklist; security@medreva.com for technical evidence?)
   3) Any NDA/attestation form Procurement requires before we can share full SOC artifacts? We can drop a redacted SOC2 report or the SOC2 summary right away; full report typically requires an NDA.
C) Tech specifics — quick bullets you can confirm now
   4) Expected average and peak daily API calls for pilot (helps us size a Dedicated node if needed).
   5) Retention window for logs and request payloads (if any) — we can disable storage or configure short retention.

We’ll start a SIG-prefill draft as soon as you confirm A1 and B2 so we don’t misstate storage assumptions. I’ll attach an internal draft of our SIG answers (redwood_sig_answers_draft.docx) and mark controls we can auto-answer versus items requiring evidence.

Proposed timeline: Karthik/Redwood to return prefilling + top-10-controls one-pager by EOD 2026-12-16 if we get scope confirmation today; otherwise target 2026-12-20.

Hi Simon / team — Marissa from Redwood Security. A few technical clarifications and what we can provide quickly:

- Encryption at rest: AES-256 for all customer data by default. We support customer-managed keys via major KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS); option to rotate keys on a schedule. We’ll note this in the SIG prefilling.
- Encryption in transit: TLS 1.2+; we enforce TLS for all endpoints.
- Customer-managed networking: Private endpoints + VPC peering available on Dedicated and Private offerings; Hosted API supports IP allowlists and private link in select regions.
- Multitenancy: Hosted API is logically multi-tenant with strong namespace isolation; Dedicated/Private can be single-tenant — we’ll mark tenant isolation options per your deployment preference.
- Logging/retention: By default we retain request metadata for 30 days; we can offer shorter retention windows and disable persistent payload storage on request for pilot.
- SOC 2 artifacts: we can provide a SOC 2 summary and controls mapping immediately. Full attested report requires a standard NDA; if you can sign an NDA we can provide the report under usual redaction rules.

Suggested evidence owners on the Redwood side: Naomi Feldman (infra/networking evidence), Jordan Blake (product/controls mapping), Marissa Cole (security and controls). We’ll populate the SIG sheet with answers we own and flag items that require customer- or third-party evidence.

Next steps (concrete):
1) Karthik: confirm scope A1 (transient PHI vs stored PHI) so we can select correct answers.
2) MedReva: confirm legal contact (Priya) for BAA routing and whether an NDA will be signed for SOC2 report.
3) Redwood: return prefilling (attached draft) + top-10-controls one-pager by 2026-12-16 if scope confirmed; otherwise 2026-12-20.

Happy to jump on a 20m follow-up call if your security team prefers to walk the SIG answers live.

—Marissa Cole
